material_systems.name: PVA Drywall Primer System
material_systems.description: Standard PVA (polyvinyl acetate) primer for sealing bare drywall. Economical, fast-drying, excellent for equalizing porosity between paper face and joint compound.

coat_stages.purpose: Seal bare drywall, equalize porosity, prevent flashing at joints

material_systems.notes: Standard system for all quality tiers. QT5 may opt for high-build primer instead.

material_systems.name: High-Build Drywall Primer System
material_systems.description: High-build primer for premium Level 5 appearance or surfaces with minor imperfections. Provides thicker film build for enhanced hiding and smoother finish.

coat_stages.purpose: Enhanced sealing and filling for premium finish preparation

material_systems.notes: Optional upgrade for QT5 projects requiring Level 5 appearance. Higher material cost.

coverage_profiles.notes: Bare drywall is absorbent. First coat consumption higher than repaint. Conservative estimate accounts for paper face absorption and joint compound areas.
High-build primers have lower coverage due to thicker film build. Higher material consumption expected.

consumable_usage_models.name: Roller Cover - Primer Application
consumable_usage_models.description: 3/8" to 1/2" nap roller cover for smooth drywall primer application
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: One cover per ~2000 SF. Replace when loaded with dried primer or nap degraded. 3/8" nap for smooth finish, 1/2" for slightly textured.

consumable_usage_models.name: Roller Frame
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: Durable item. One frame covers large area unless damaged.

consumable_usage_models.name: Extension Pole
consumable_usage_models.description: Telescoping extension pole for ceiling roller work
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: Reusable equipment. One per crew member working ceilings.

consumable_usage_models.name: Brush - Cut-In
consumable_usage_models.description: 2.5" to 3" angled sash brush for cut-in work
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: One brush per ~5000 LF of cut-in. Quality brush recommended for clean lines.

consumable_usage_models.name: Airless Spray Tip
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: One tip per ~50 gallons sprayed. Replace when fan pattern degrades.

consumable_usage_models.name: Spray Gun Filter
consumable_usage_models.description: Mesh filter for airless spray gun
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: Replace when clogged. More frequent replacement with dusty primer.

consumable_usage_models.name: Sandpaper/Sanding Sponge - Fine Grit
consumable_usage_models.description: 150-180 grit sandpaper or sanding sponge for post-prime sanding
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: One sheet/sponge per ~500 SF. Light hand sanding only.

consumable_usage_models.name: Tack Cloth
consumable_usage_models.description: Tack cloth for removing sanding dust
consumable_usage_models.usage_notes: Use after sanding to remove dust before topcoat.

consumable_usage_models.name: Duster/Dust Brush
consumable_usage_models.description: Dust brush or duster for pre-prime surface prep

materials_catalog.description: PVA drywall primer - seals bare drywall, equalizes porosity
typical_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec 500 Interior Primer
Behr Premium Plus Interior Drywall Primer
materials_catalog.notes: Generic PVA primers are acceptable. No specific brand required for standard new construction.

materials_catalog.description: High-build drywall primer for Level 5 finish preparation
typical_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec 500 High Build Primer
materials_catalog.notes: Higher cost. Used for premium finishes or imperfect surfaces.

compatibility_rules.description: PVA primer compatible with all latex topcoats
compatibility_rules.notes: Standard compatibility. Allow proper dry time before topcoat.

compatibility_rules.description: High-build primer compatible with all latex topcoats
compatibility_rules.notes: Allow extended dry time per manufacturer specs.
PVA primer acceptable under oil-based topcoats if fully cured. Verify with topcoat manufacturer.

risk_notes.description: Flashing at joints if primer coverage insufficient
risk_notes.mitigation: Ensure adequate mil build. Inspect before topcoat. Touch-up thin areas.

risk_notes.description: Adhesion failure if drywall dusty or damp
risk_notes.mitigation: Dust surfaces before priming. Verify drywall is dry (moisture meter if uncertain).

risk_notes.description: Poor backroll adhesion if primer allowed to dry before backrolling
risk_notes.mitigation: Maintain wet-on-wet backroll. Do not allow spray to flash before backroll.

assumptions: Coverage rates assume Level 4 drywall finish with standard porosity
Consumable usage rates are estimates - actual may vary by technique and conditions
Material pricing is not defined at spec level - handled by runtime pricing module
Spray equipment (sprayer, hoses) is crew equipment, not per-project consumable
uncertainty_flags: High-build primer coverage rate may vary significantly by product and application technique
Consumable lifespan varies by brand quality and user technique
